chapter: Records, Lovie Austin and a first marriage
title: Townsend's later success as Redcaps president
summary: He wrote her during Show Boat thanking her, became president of the Redcaps and CIO board member, and they stayed platonic friends until he died.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: So when I opened in Showboat -- I must tell you this -- when I was in Showboat --

-- in London, yes -- I received a letter from him saying he just didn't -- a note to the woman who had won. He didn't want to prove on my success and all, but just a note to the woman who had won, because he had gone to school in Canada and got a degree in commercial --

-- art -- no, no, not commercial art, commercial -- business, you know, because he became the president of the Redcaps here in New York. See? He said, just a note, because, you know, to the woman who had won

because of my success in making him a success, because had I let him hang around, you know, and not do any work and just hang around there and accept the nickels and dimes from the people where I'm singing, you know, he would have never made a man of himself. So I made a man of him.

See? And he became -- oh, he was quite a big man, because when I -- this is, you know, after, but when I was in Tokyo, I was going to Yokahama, and we crossed on the ocean. He was going to attend to some business for the commercial -- the Redcaps -- they didn't call them Redcaps, but anyhow --
Well, they didn't call them porters. Anyhow, the redcaps -- it was the redcaps.
Yes, he was the president of it. He was going to do business over in -- there for the union because he was the only Negro on the executive board of the CIO. So I helped him a lot, didn't I?

Yeah. And we were the best of friends. We were the -- when I came back from Europe and all, we used to go out to dinner and all and just good platonic friends. But we used to talk of my success and his, and he finally died.

He died, uh-huh. But he was a wonderful young man. He was a fine young man. And his father -- his grandfather, poor old man, used to come while I was in Cincinnati with a little basket on his arms bringing me vegetables out of the garden. Wasn't that lovely?
